info.title: ScrapeUnblocker API
info.description: Public API for the ScrapeUnblocker proxy/anti-bot service. Authenticate every request with the `x-scrapeunblocker-key` header. Three endpoints are documented here: page-source extraction, Google SERP scraping, and image fetch. All other paths exist for internal operations and are intentionally hidden from this spec.

post.summary: Fetch the HTML (or parsed JSON) for any URL
post.description: Routes the URL through the appropriate anti-bot bypass chain (custom domain plugins, super-profile browser, residential proxies). Returns the prettified HTML by default. Set `parsed_data=true` to receive a structured JSON payload extracted via Schema.org / __NEXT_DATA__ / AI-generated rules; the response body becomes `{ "data": { page_type, source, data } }` instead of HTML. Use `get_cookies=true` to additionally receive cookies and the proxy address that served the request.

200.description: Success — body is HTML (or JSON when `parsed_data=true` / `get_cookies=true`). Also a dead-origin 5xx page, as served (can be empty): then the `X-Origin-Status` header carries the target's status. Billed.

400.description: Invalid URL, unsupported scheme or `proxy_country`, or `Hostname cannot be resolved` - the domain does not exist (billed).

404.description: The target itself answered 404 (the page does not exist). The body is the target's own page, as served (can be empty), and `X-Origin-Status: 404` tells it apart from a wrong API path. Billed - retrying returns the same answer.

410.description: The target itself answered 410 (the page is gone). Same shape as 404: the target's page with `X-Origin-Status: 410`. Billed.

403.description: Blocked by bot protection on every available bypass path.

415.description: The URL is not an HTML document (image, PDF, file); use /getImage for images. Not billed.

422.description: Validation error, or `no_data_extracted`: with `parsed_data=true` the page rendered but no structured data could be extracted (no HTML returned). Not billed.

503.description: No render capacity on our side right now; not the target's fault, not billed - retry with backoff.

504.description: Request timed out: the call reached its time cap (60 s, 90 s with `steps`). Not billed.

523.description: Origin unreachable (target down or flapping, or our origin breaker is open); not a bot block, not billed - retry later.

post.summary: Scrape a Google search SERP for organic + ad results

Set `pages_to_check` 1-10 to paginate. `wait_after_load` adds a delay after the SERP loads (useful for sites where ads render late); `captcha_pause` lets you eyeball / solve a CAPTCHA when running interactively.

403.description: Google CAPTCHA after retries with different proxies — try another `proxy_country`.

Filter with `condition`, `listing_type`, `min_price`/`max_price`, `free_shipping`, `seller` or `category`, sort with `sort`, and page with `page`/`page_size` (60, 120 or 240 per page). Set `marketplace` to search a specific site - prices, currency and availability differ between ebay.com, ebay.de, ebay.co.uk and the rest.

When eBay finds no exact match it still serves a full page of its own loosely-related suggestions. That case is reported honestly: `exactMatches` is `false` and a `notice` explains it, so those listings are never mistaken for real matches.

post.description:
Returns an Amazon ranked list for a category on any regional marketplace: Best Sellers (default), New Releases, Movers & Shakers, Most Wished For or Gift Ideas (`list_type`). The response carries the `category` (`name`, `slug`, `nodeId`, `url`, `parents`, `subcategories` - each with a url you can pass back as `category`) and up to `max_results` ranked `items`: `rank`, `asin`, `title`, `url`, `image`, `price` + `currency`, `offersCount`, `rating`, `reviewsCount`, and on Movers & Shakers `salesRank`, `previousSalesRank` and `salesRankChangePct`.

Pass `category` as a department slug (`electronics`), slug plus browse-node id (`electronics/172541`) or a pasted Amazon list url; leave it empty for the all-departments root (department list, no items). A list holds up to 100 items over two pages of 50, and each page fetched is billed as one request. When Amazon has no list for a category it says so, and that text is returned in `message` with an empty `items` array. An item whose card Amazon did not load (it loads ranks 31-50 of each page lazily) comes back with only `rank`, `asin` and `url`; `itemsWithDetails` counts the complete ones.

`proxy_country` defaults to the marketplace's home country (amazon.com -> US) so prices are in the store's currency.

Empty = the all-departments root, which returns the department list (`category.subcategories`) and no items.

post.description: Given an Airbnb `room` (listing id or room URL), returns its guest `reviews`: `id`, `rating`, `text` (as written) with its `language`, `translatedText` (Airbnb's translation into `locale`), `date` (ISO), `localizedDate`, `stayDetail`, `photos`, `reviewer` (`id`, `name`, `photo`, `location` or `tenure`, `profileUrl`, `profileId`, `isSuperhost`, `deleted`) and the host's `response`. `reviewer.id` is Airbnb's account id (the one in its photo URLs; airbnb.com/users/show/<id> asks anonymous visitors to log in), while `profileUrl` is the public profile link Airbnb's own review cards open, keyed by a separate public id given as `profileId`. `deleted` is true when the guest has since closed their Airbnb account; Airbnb still sends the name, photo and location or tenure from the review, and they are returned as sent. post.description: Returns a company's Glassdoor employee reviews as JSON. Each review has `id`, `url`, `title`, `rating` (1-5), `subratings` (work/life balance, culture and values, diversity and inclusion, career opportunities, compensation and benefits, senior management), `recommendToFriend`, `ceoApproval`, `businessOutlook`, `pros`, `cons`, `advice`, `jobTitle`, `employmentStatus`, `isCurrentEmployee`, `yearsOfEmployment`, `location`, `date`, `helpfulCount`, `notHelpfulCount`, `featured`, `employerResponse` and `view` (the sort / filter view it came from). The response also carries `summary` (overall rating, review counts, recommend / CEO approval / business outlook percentages, the CEO, sub-rating averages, star distribution, reviews in the last 7 and 30 days), `companyMeta` (name, logo, website, industry, sector, headquarters, size) and `totalReviews`. The counts are Glassdoor's own and measure different sets: `totalReviews` is the number of reviews matching every filter of the call (`rating`, `job_title`, `keyword`, `topic`, `employment_status`, `language`, `current_only`; the default view is English reviews by full-time and part-time employees), the set the views read from. `summary.allReviewsCount` is every review Glassdoor holds for the employer, rated or not, in any language and employment status; no filter changes it. `summary.reviewCount` is the number of ratings behind `summary.overallRating`, and `summary.ratedReviewsCount` the number of reviews that carry a star rating; Glassdoor counts the two separately, so they can differ by a few. Both follow `rating` but not the language or employment filters, so they are usually above `totalReviews`. `summary.ratingDistribution` holds the star counts Glassdoor sends for its rating bars (`overall`, each sub-rating, and `recommendToFriend`); for employers with many reviews they cover only part of them (Google: 18,643 overall against a `reviewCount` of 52,845), so read them as proportions, not totals, and with `rating` set only that star is counted. `summary.reviewsLast7Days` and `reviewsLast30Days` count reviews matching the filters. Give `company` as a Glassdoor employer id, a Glassdoor company URL or a company name. Only US exits are used (`proxy_country` accepts US or blank): Glassdoor redirects other countries to their local site, where these pages do not exist. Glassdoor shows anonymous visitors only the first page (3 reviews) of each sort / filter view and redirects deeper pages to sign-in, so there is no page parameter: use `sort`, `rating` and the filters to reach other reviews, or raise `max_results` to read several views in one call. `hasMore` is always false and `nextPage` null; `publicLimitReached` is true when fewer reviews came back than asked because the views anonymous visitors may read ran out.
